title: Why Smith theory imposes no rational obstruction for free Z/2-actions
question: Let X be a finite CW-complex that is rationally acyclic (H_i(X;\mathbb Q)=0 for i>0) and let \tau act cellularly with \tau^2=1. Classical Smith theory says that the fixed set X^{\langle\tau\rangle} controls H_*(X;\mathbb Z/2), and many texts conclude that Z/2-actions on mod-2 acyclic complexes have fixed points. Why does this argument fail over \mathbb Q? More concretely, how do transfer and averaging show that a free \mathbb Z/2-action on a rationally acyclic space produces no obstruction, even though the mod-2 Smith inequalities still hold?
answer: Smith theory is inherently p-local: the Smith chains are the subcomplexes of the cellular chain complex C_*(X;\mathbb F_p) obtained by restricting and averaging with respect to \tau. When the coefficient field has characteristic p, the operator 1+\tau is nilpotent, so one obtains a long exact sequence relating H_*(X;\mathbb F_p) to H_*(X^{\langle\tau\rangle};\mathbb F_p), forcing nontrivial fixed-point homology whenever X is mod-p acyclic. In characteristic zero, 1+\tau is invertible, and the same chain-level argument collapses. Instead we have a transfer map tr:H_*(X/\tau;\mathbb Q)\to H_*(X;\mathbb Q) defined by averaging preimages, and it satisfies tr\circ\pi_*=2\,id_{H_*(X;\mathbb Q)}. Because 2 is invertible in \mathbb Q, \pi_* is injective and every class in H_*(X;\mathbb Q) is 2 times the transfer of a class downstairs. Thus H_*(X;\mathbb Q) carries no information about X^{\langle\tau\rangle}.\n\nIf the action is free, \pi:X\to X/\tau is a covering of degree 2 and the transfer shows H_*(X/\tau;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(X;\mathbb Q)^\tau. For a rationally acyclic X this invariant subspace vanishes, so X/\tau is also rationally acyclic and there is no contradiction with Smith theory. The only nontrivial constraints live in mod-2 homology, where 2 is no longer invertible: there the Smith complex detects fixed-point data through the short exact sequence 0\to C_*(X^{\langle\tau\rangle};\mathbb F_2)\to C_*(X;\mathbb F_2)\xrightarrow{1+\tau} C_*(X;\mathbb F_2)\to 0. Consequently, mod-2 Smith theory continues to impose fixed-point obstructions, but rational coefficients bypass them entirely because averaging by 1/2 kills the obstruction.
